plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs that light up the winter garden with rose-like blooms in layers of silky petals around golden stamens. Their dark, polished leaves make the flowers look even brighter against the cold season's muted backdrop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with peak flowering in mid-winter
plants.location: Japan, and mild-winter gardens in the southeastern United States and western Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Both belong to the same genus.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low, clump-forming woodland perennial that opens nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with a boss of yellow stamens in the depths of winter. The blooms often push up through frost and light snow, and they age to a soft blush pink.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring, often opening around Christmas
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of the Alps and Apennines in central and southern Europe, and widely grown in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, this plant is not a true rose. It belongs to the buttercup family, and all parts of it are toxic.

plants.name: Nuytsia floribunda
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere summer, this tree covers itself in huge clusters of bright orange flowers. The display is so dense that whole trees seem to glow against the sandy bushland.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to mid-summer, peaking in December and January
plants.funFact: It is the world's largest parasitic plant. Its roots tap into the roots of neighboring plants, and it has been known to grow into buried cables, apparently mistaking them for roots.
